newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Cardo says EU approves Thyssen rail merger.
newsitem.headline: Cardo says EU approves Thyssen rail merger.

text.p: Swedish engineering company Cardo AB on Monday said it had received approval from the European Union to merge its rail brake systems operation with a similar unit at Thyssen AG.
The approval means that Cardo and Thyssen will create a joint venture called Cardo BSI Rail AB, which will be operational from the beginning of 1997, Cardo said in a statement.
Cardo said it will hold 60 percent in the new company, which will be based in Malmo, southern Sweden.
The approval follows an agreement in principle between the two companies in March this year and a final agreement in September.
The merger means the creation of one of the world's largest railway industry subcontractors, Cardo said.
After the merger, Cardo Railway will have annual sales of around 2.5 billion crowns and the number of employees will total about 2,400, the company said.
Cardo said the merger would mean significant synergies within product development, manufacturing and marketing.
